theorem_title: Finite Minkowski allocation from exact primal-dual support budgets
formal_statement:
namespace Hirsch
theorem finite_allocation_minkowski_primal_dual_budgets
    {E : Type*} [NormedAddCommGroup E] [NormedSpace ℝ E]
    (m k : ℕ) (a : Fin m → E →L[ℝ] ℝ)
    (G : (Fin k → ℝ) →L[ℝ] E) :
    ∃ c : Finset (Fin m ⊕ Option (Fin k)) → ((Fin m ⊕ Option (Fin k)) → ℝ),
      (∀ s, (∀ i, 0 ≤ c s i) ∧
        ∀ j, -(∑ i, c s (.inl i) * a i (G (Pi.single j (1 : ℝ)))) -
          c s (.inr (some j)) + c s (.inr none) = 0) ∧
      ∀ (b h : Fin m → ℝ) (t : ℝ), 0 ≤ t →
        (∀ θ : Fin k → ℝ, (∀ j, 0 ≤ θ j) → (∑ j, θ j) ≤ t →
          ∀ i, a i (G θ) ≤ h i) →
        ∀ (alpha : Finset (Fin m ⊕ Option (Fin k)) → Fin m → ℝ)
          (xstar : Finset (Fin m ⊕ Option (Fin k)) → E),
          (∀ s i, 0 ≤ alpha s i) →
          (∀ s i, a i (xstar s) ≤ b i) →
          (∀ s x : E,
            (∑ i, c s (.inl i) * a i x) = ∑ i, alpha s i * a i x) →
          (∀ s i, alpha s i * (b i - a i (xstar s)) = 0) →
          (({x : E | ∀ i, a i x ≤ b i} =
            {x : E | ∃ p : E, (∀ i, a i p ≤ b i - h i) ∧
              ∃ θ : Fin k → ℝ, (∀ j, 0 ≤ θ j) ∧ (∑ j, θ j) ≤ t ∧ p + G θ = x}) ↔
            ∀ s,
              (∑ i, c s (.inl i) * h i) - c s (.inr none) * t ≤
                (∑ i, c s (.inl i) * b i) - ∑ i, alpha s i * b i) := by sorry
end Hirsch
natural_language_statement:
Let a finite H-system be given by continuous linear rows $a_i(x)\le b_i$, and let $G$ map a bounded allocation simplex $\{\theta\ge0:\sum_j\theta_j\le t\}$ into a finite-generator candidate summand. There is a fixed finite family of nonnegative allocation-null multipliers $c_s=(\lambda_s,\mu_s,\nu_s)$ depending only on the row map and $G$. Assume the candidate has rowwise support bounds $h_i$. For each fixed multiplier $s$, also supply a feasible original point $x_s^*$ and nonnegative original-row dual weights $\alpha_s$ representing the same objective as $\lambda_s$, with complementary slackness at $x_s^*$. Then whole-set Minkowski reconstruction by the erosion is equivalent to the finite scalar family

$$
\sum_i\lambda_{s,i}h_i-\nu_s t\le\sum_i\lambda_{s,i}b_i-\sum_i\alpha_{s,i}b_i\qquad\text{for every }s.
$$

Thus the universal quantifier over every original feasible point in the finite allocation criterion is eliminated exactly when primal/dual support witnesses are supplied. The theorem does not construct those witnesses, certify an LP implementation, discover summands, or bound graph diameter.
